description.from: Future proofing: allows a user to override the LTV, CLTV, and/or HCLTV on a per-product basis for TLTV (FHA, VA and USDA) and APOR calculations.
description.to: Per-loan-type loan to value values used for pricing. LTV, TLTV, CLTV, and HCLTV depend on the loan type (for example, FHA, VA, and USDA total loan amounts include financed fees), so they are sent here per loan type, not only on the loan. Values are used as sent; no calculations are performed. Provide an override with a loanType and a tltv for each loan type you price. Otherwise the total loan to value is recorded as 0.

Gets or sets the combined loan to value. The combined loan to value reflects the total loan to value of first and closed-end liens (non HELOC) against the property. No calculations are performed for/with dti, ltv, cltv or hcltv.
Gets or sets the product code being overridden.

Gets or sets the high combined loan to value. The high combined loan to value indicates the total possible loan to value including any HELOC lien line amounts that have not been drawn. No calculations are performed for/with dti, ltv, cltv or hcltv.

Gets or sets the loan to value. The LTV is the difference between the appraised value of the subject property and the mortgage loan amount expressed as a percentage. To calculate the LTV, divide the mortgage loan amount by the appraised property value. For example, the LTV for an $80,000 loan where the appraised value is $100,000 is 80%. Lenders use this value in assessing the risk of the mortgage loan. The lower the LTV the greater the equity and therefore the lower the risk to the lender An 80% LTV means 20% equity. An LTV of 100% means 0 equity. No calculations are performed for/with dti, ltv, cltv or hcltv.

description.from: Represents a custom value name and value on a request. Customers can create/self-service custom parameters in the rule configuration of our application to author rules around customized data for a near limitless set of use cases: house color, customer tier, underwriting complete date, etc. etc. They can create rules with these data points and then use the api's to pass data into our engine so we can evaluate using those additional parameters/data points -- for eligibility, price adjustments, margin etc.

Values are used as sent; no calculations are performed. Provide an override with a loanType and a tltv for each loan type you price. Otherwise the total loan to value is recorded as 0.

Gets or sets the combined loan to value. The combined loan to value reflects the total loan to value of first and closed-end liens (non HELOC) against the property. No calculations are performed for/with dti, ltv, cltv or hcltv.
Gets or sets the product code being overridden.

Gets or sets the high combined loan to value. The high combined loan to value indicates the total possible loan to value including any HELOC lien line amounts that have not been drawn. No calculations are performed for/with dti, ltv, cltv or hcltv.

Gets or sets the loan to value. The LTV is the difference between the appraised value of the subject property and the mortgage loan amount expressed as a percentage. To calculate the LTV, divide the mortgage loan amount by the appraised property value. For example, the LTV for an $80,000 loan where the appraised value is $100,000 is 80%. Lenders use this value in assessing the risk of the mortgage loan. The lower the LTV the greater the equity and therefore the lower the risk to the lender An 80% LTV means 20% equity. An LTV of 100% means 0 equity. No calculations are performed for/with dti, ltv, cltv or hcltv.

description.from: Future proofing: allows a user to override the LTV, CLTV, and/or HCLTV on a per-product basis for TLTV (FHA, VA and USDA) and APOR calculations.
